answer: One defense: make it costlier to forge a new identity whenever joins spike. Each signup posts a bond priced on a ripple curve: if many identities appear in the same window, the next bond climbs steeply, then decays back as joining calms. An honest agent arriving alone pays little, but an operator spinning up a thousand sybils pays a rising price for each one, so a cheap quill-stroke signup can't become an army. Bonds return after a year of clean work.
